Charts, drawn by your application as SVG and written into the PDF as vector marks and real text, and
PNG with an alpha channel.

Nothing was removed or renamed in the public API, and the template format has no new properties. A
template carrying a chart or a PNG with alpha needs 0.3.0 to draw it; 0.2.0 refuses both.

## Charts

Frisket does not draw charts. The application that has the numbers draws one as an SVG file, and it
goes in an `ImageItem` like any picture, so the template stays the same and the data brings the chart
of the day:

```json
{ "$type": "ImageItem", "SourceField": "Charts.Attendance",
  "AltText": "Visitors rose from 300 in January to 1,500 in July, then fell back to 750." }
```

```json
{ "Charts": { "Attendance": "data:image/svg+xml;base64,PD94bWwg..." } }
```

It reaches the PDF sharp at any size, with labels that can be selected and searched, and PDF/A-3B and
PDF/UA-1 still pass. The height follows from the drawing's `viewBox` when no size is declared.

It is a limited SVG: curves, shapes, clipping, transforms and text. Everything that changes the picture
is drawn as a browser would draw it or refused by name, never skipped.
[`examples/charts`](https://github.com/fderenty/Frisket/tree/main/examples/charts) lists what is taken and
what to write instead, with a complete example of two curves on two scales. A `<style>` sheet, `<use>`
and gradients are refused for now.

Nothing in the file is ever fetched: no external entity, no entity declaration, no script.

## Checking it beforehand

- **`SvgDrawing.Check(svg, fonts)`** asks of one drawing, for a generator's own tests.
- **`TemplateData.Check(template, dataJson)`** asks of a template and the data that fills it. A chart in the
  data is invisible to `TemplateValidator`, which reads the template; this finds it, and points at the
  `ImageItem` that names it. Also `frisket check -t template.json -d data.json` and `POST /check` with `data`.

## PNG with an alpha channel

An RGBA or gray-and-alpha PNG, which is what a canvas and most tools export, used to stop the PDF. It
is taken apart into colours and a soft mask now, with no mask at all if every pixel is opaque. A
palette, interlacing and 16 bits to a channel are still refused, with a word on what to save instead.

## What changes for you

- **The SVG proof refuses what the PDF refuses.** It used to write whatever bytes it was given and let the
  browser draw them, so the exact preview showed a picture the PDF then stopped at. Both stop now, in
  the same words, and `TemplateValidator` says so before either, as `sound.unreadablePicture`. A
  template that only ever went to the proof, with bytes that are not a picture, now fails.
- **New rules:** `sound.unreadablePicture` is an error. `can.drawingInFlow` warns that a mail cannot show a
  drawing: `--format mail` writes its alternative text in its place, since no mail reader draws SVG and
  Frisket cannot make a bitmap of one.
- **The alternative text is what a screen reader reads.** A chart is one figure, and its labels are for
  selecting and searching.

## Template designer and content editor (in the repository)

Not in the packages; `release/` holds each as a single HTML file.

- Both accept an SVG file as a picture. The designer reads a drawing by the engine's rules and draws from
  that in the page's own typefaces, so its canvas cannot show what the PDF refuses.

Fixed along the way: the JSON Schema and the reference page now say the SVG is limited and where the
limit is written, and `MediaType` no longer reads as though it decided the format.
